- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.77) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.23) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk aversion or market panic.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days); apply smoothing or lagged decay to prevent overcorrection.
- In mean-reversion regimes (sentiment neutral or mildly negative), model often holds too low; raise forecast toward historical mean or 30-day moving average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to underestimate late-period price action (especially after sentiment shifts); add 1–2% buffer for tail risk or momentum carry.
- If sentiment shows strong upward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive positive values), model often fails to capture momentum; increase forecast slope or add 0.5–1.0% premium.
- When sentiment is mixed or oscillating, model tends to average out; use sentiment-weighted median or trimmed mean to reduce noise.
